# pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster (Data Source)

Looks up one existing Kubernetes cluster by id or name, to read its version, network, size, autoscaling range, API server endpoint and allow-list, or volume storage without managing it. It does not expose the kubeconfig: manage the cluster with pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster, or download the kubeconfig from the console or the API. Failed and deleted clusters are not found.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look an existing cluster up by name (or by id). Names are unique in the
# organization. The lookup exposes metadata only, never the kubeconfig.
data "pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster" "prod" {
  name = "prod"
}

output "prod_cluster" {
  value = {
    version  = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.kubernetes_version
    workers  = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.workers
    upgrades = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.available_upgrade_ids
    # enabled, min_workers and max_workers (both 0 when autoscaling is off)
    autoscaling       = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.autoscaling
    endpoint          = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.endpoint
    api_allowed_cidrs = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.api_allowed_cidrs
    volume_storage_gb = data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.volume_storage_gb
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Id of the Kubernetes cluster to look up, starting with k8s_. Set exactly one of id and name.
- `name` (String) Name of the Kubernetes cluster to look up. It must match exactly. Names are unique in the account. Set exactly one of id and name.

### Read-Only

- `api_allowed_cidrs` (List of String) IPv4 CIDRs allowed to reach the API server, sorted. Empty means any address.
- `autoscaling` (Attributes) The cluster autoscaler. When enabled it moves workers between min_workers and max_workers; when not, both bounds are 0. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `available_upgrade_ids` (List of String) Ids of the Kubernetes versions the cluster can be upgraded to now.
- `control_nodes` (Number) Control plane nodes: 1, or 3 for a highly available control plane.
- `created_at` (String) When the cluster was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `endpoint` (String) The API server's URL. Null until the cluster has one.
- `in_sync` (Boolean) False while a scale or upgrade has not finished.
- `kubernetes_version` (String) The Kubernetes version the cluster runs, for example "1.31.2".
- `kubernetes_version_id` (String) Id of the Kubernetes version the cluster runs.
- `network_id` (String) Id of the VPC network the nodes are in. Null in a standard zone.
- `node` (Attributes) Size of every node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node))
- `node_plan_id` (String) Id of the plan every node uses.
- `nodes` (Number) control_nodes plus workers: the number of VMs billed.
- `observed_state` (String) State of the cluster as the platform sees it, for example "running".
- `subnet_id` (String) Id of the subnet the nodes are in. Null in a standard zone.
- `volume_storage_gb` (Number) Storage, in GB, that the workloads' persistent volume claims use, billed with the nodes' disks.
- `workers` (Number) Worker nodes.
- `zone_id` (String) Zone the cluster is in.

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the autoscaler runs.
- `max_workers` (Number) Most workers, or 0 when autoscaling is off.
- `min_workers` (Number) Fewest workers, or 0 when autoscaling is off.


<a id="nestedatt--node"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node`

Read-Only:

- `disk_gb` (Number) Disk, in GB.
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory, in MB.
- `vcpu` (Number) Virtual CPUs.
